title: Sainsbury’s store pauses AI scanning after false shoplifting accusation

paragraphs.en: Sainsbury’s has paused the use of AI face scanning in one of its stores after a customer was wrongly identified as a shoplifter and ejected from the shop.
paragraphs.zh: 在一位顾客被错误识别为小偷并被赶出商店后，塞恩斯伯里（Sainsbury's）已在一家门店暂停使用人工智能面部扫描技术。

paragraphs.en: “I was embarrassed, mortified even, and felt quite humiliated and powerless,” Matt Arnold, 46, said of his ordeal.
paragraphs.zh: “我感到尴尬，甚至难堪，感到相当羞辱和无能为力，”46岁的马特·阿诺德（Matt Arnold）谈及自己的遭遇时说。

paragraphs.en: The comedy promoter was buying supplies in the store in East Dulwich, in south-east London, for a standup event at Dulwich Hamlet football club when, after scanning his items and a Nectar card, he was approached by two managers who told him he could not be served owing to an earlier incident. He was then asked to leave and they tried to escort him from the store.
paragraphs.zh: 这位喜剧演出经纪人当时正在伦敦东南部东达利奇（East Dulwich）的这家门店，为在达利奇哈姆雷特（Dulwich Hamlet）足球俱乐部举办的脱口秀活动采购物资。扫描完商品和一张Nectar积分卡后，两名经理走近他，告诉他因之前的一起事件而不能为他服务，随后要求他离开，并试图把他带出商店。

paragraphs.en: “They simply told me they would be walking me out,” Arnold said. “At that point I did stand my ground and said I would be walking myself out. I was determined to keep some dignity. On this point, if nothing else, they did relent.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们只是告诉我，会把我带出去，”阿诺德说，“当时我坚持立场，说自己会走出去。我决心保住一些尊严。在这一点上，不管怎样，他们确实退让了。”

paragraphs.en: As he left, he saw an overhead CCTV monitor alert with a red circle surrounding his face. He asked the shop staff to keep his shopping in the trolley so his friend could come and pick up the supplies for the comedy night happening soon next door.
paragraphs.zh: 离开时，他看到一个头顶的闭路电视监控警报，上面有一个红圈圈住他的脸。他请店员把购物留在购物车里，以便朋友随后过来取走物资，用于即将在隔壁举行的喜剧之夜活动。

paragraphs.en: “I think they were quite confused by this, understandably, but agreed and my colleague Dave went in to pay for and pick up the shop about five minutes later. There was no pause for thought from the staff, no suggestion that they understood this is not how a shoplifter would behave. Just blindly following the machine’s orders.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想他们对此相当困惑，这也可以理解，但他们还是同意了。大约五分钟后，我的同事戴夫进店付款并取走了商品。员工们没有片刻思考，似乎也不明白小偷不会这样行事。他们只是盲目听从机器的指令。”

paragraphs.en: Sainsbury’s head office apologised to Arnold the next day and has paused use of its AI-assisted Facewatch technology in the store while an investigation takes place. But Arnold says the technology should be paused in all stores and he is worried about the extent to which AI is being used in society.
paragraphs.zh: 次日，塞恩斯伯里总部向阿诺德道歉，并在调查进行期间暂停在该门店使用其人工智能辅助的Facewatch技术。但阿诺德表示，这项技术应在所有门店暂停使用，他担心人工智能在社会中的使用程度。

paragraphs.en: “Anyone could be falsely accused and at some point that will be someone vulnerable, someone with mental health issues like anxiety. It’s inevitable,” he said. “Also, I would worry about the confidence-destroying effect of it happening to a younger person or someone less willing or able to stand up for themselves as I have done.”
paragraphs.zh: “任何人都可能被冤枉，而总有一天这会落在某个弱势群体身上，某个像焦虑症这样有心理健康问题的人身上。这是不可避免的，”他说，“此外，我担心如果这种事发生在一个年轻人，或某个不像我这样愿意、能够为自己挺身而出的人身上，会摧毁他们的自信。”
